email.subject: How to finish a relief carving: the complete guide
email.intro:
Most relief carvings are lost after the machine finishes, not during the cut.

A carving is a landscape of very small hills and valleys, and the only reason anyone can see it is that light falls across it and leaves shadows. Fill those valleys with thick varnish and the whole thing goes flat. Keep them dark and the same board looks like it came out of a church.

We have just published the long version of how to do that, and there is one step that does most of the work. Flood the carving with a dark glaze, then wipe it back off the raised surfaces only. Here it is, half finished:
